model: Life insurer FCFE at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 5.8% vs EPS 5-yr CAGR 25.2%: diverges >30%. Two causes: (1) the IFRS 4 -> IFRS 17/9 transition on 1 Jan 2023 restated FY2022 equity from 436,169 to 366,021 and net profit from 32,082 to 66,680, so any CAGR spanning FY2022 mixes bases; (2) FY2024-FY2025 EPS is peak-cycle (realised + unrealised gains 196bn in FY2025 vs a 4-yr average far lower). The 3-yr figures are on the restated IFRS 17 base (FY2022 revenue 370,861, NI 66,680, equity 366,021) but still end on the FY2025 peak. The selected 6% is the dividend and book-value compounding rate, deliberately NOT the EPS rate.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use dividends declared as the FCFE series (the model's definition of owner cash flow for an insurer), not OCF: DPS FY2020 0.64, FY2022 0.49, FY2025 0.856. Revenue 5-yr is null because FY2020 (IFRS 4, 804,961) and FY2025 (IFRS 17, 616,065) are not the same quantity. SBC is zero in every year, so the owner-FCF SBC adjustment does not arise.

scenario_narratives.base: Peak-cycle FY2025/H1 2026 earnings normalise in FY2027 to ~RMB98bn (ROE ~14%); investment assets and CSM release grow the book 5-6.5% a year; payout rises from 17% to 45% over ten years as solvency stays comfortably above 150%. Cost of equity 10% CNY.
scenario_narratives.bull: A ~5% sustained total investment return, VNB compounding 15-20% on participating products, margin 25.5%, payout to 55%: the H-share rerates toward 0.6x EV.
scenario_narratives.bear: H2 2026 market drawdown reverses the H1 gains, then a negative-spread FY2027 at a 17% margin; growth 3-4%, payout held in the 30s. The H-share stays at ~0.25x EV.

valuation_philosophy.summary: China Life is valued on the cash a shareholder actually receives -- dividends -- discounted at a 10% CNY cost of equity, with the FY2025/H1 2026 investment-gain windfall explicitly normalised away by FY2027 rather than capitalised. The base case lands the H-share near 1.0x H1 2026 book and ~0.4x embedded value: the valuation is a bet on the payout ratio rising from 16% toward 45% as solvency allows, not on peak earnings persisting. At 0.82x book, 0.34x EV and a 4.5% trailing yield the quote already discounts a harsh H2 2026; the 43% H-discount to the A-share is structural and is not assumed to close.
key_risks_to_valuation: H2 2026 A-share reversal: 135.8bn of H1 2026 unrealised gains sit in profit under IFRS 9 FVTPL; a 10% equity-market fall roughly erases a half-year of normalised profit (bear case).
Negative spread: ~1.8% 10-year CGB against a legacy book with 3-3.5% guaranteed rates; the regulator's dynamic guaranteed-rate mechanism reprices new business only.
Payout ratio is the dominant lever: every 5pp on the terminal payout is worth roughly 10% of the base IV; the 16% FY2025 payout is the lowest in a decade and the base case assumes it nearly triples.
IFRS 17 revenue and margin are not stable quantities: total revenues can swing 20% a year on investment income, so the growth and margin paths must be read together as a net-income path.
A/H discount (43%) and capital controls: the per-share value is on the total share count; nothing in the model assumes the H-share converges on the A-share price.

State control (68.37% China Life Group): dividend policy, equity-allocation mandates ('patient capital', 'five priorities') and risk appetite are set with policy objectives alongside shareholder returns.
Solvency drawdowns under C-ROSS II: core solvency moved 128.8% -> 156.8% in six months on OCI; it can move the other way just as fast and would cap the payout.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (intraday HKEX print); 52-week range 22.46-36.16. fx from CNYHKD=X / HKDCNY=X same timestamp; A-share parity from 601628.SS.
data_sources.financials: research/2628.HK/Reports/2628.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics FY2018-FY2025, H1 FY2023-H1 FY2026) and the kpis table (EmbeddedValue, ValueOfNewBusiness, GrossWrittenPremiums, SolvencyRatio, DividendsPaid, NetIncomeInclNCI, RevenueRestated, NetIncomeRestated, InterestRevenueOnFinancialAssets); FY2025 Annual Report (2628.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt: income statement :5940-5959, investment income :1093-1104, dividends Note 30 :11000-11013, EV :1527-1532); H1 2026 interim (2628.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt: KPIs :440-470, investment income :864-880, solvency :1150-1151, dividends Note 15 :3640-3646, outlook :1222-1262).
data_sources.qualitative: No 2628.HK_Analysis.json existed at build time; business context from the FY2025 AR and H1 2026 interim MD&A directly, and from the 1336.HK (New China Life) valuation as the sector template.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 'Total revenues' under IFRS 17/9 (FY2025 AR consolidated income statement, 2628.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:5945): insurance revenue 214,136 + investment income 255,411 + associates 6,353 + other. The IFRS 17 top line is NOT premiums: GWP was 729,887 in FY2025 (+8.7%) and 536,634 in H1 2026 (+2.2%). Investment income is the swing line: of FY2025 gross investment income 387,694, net investment income was 193,795 with realised gains 132,951 and unrealised gains 63,307 (AR:1093-1104, gross yield 6.09% vs 5.50% FY2024 and 2.43% FY2023). H1 2026 total revenues 434,563 (+81.5%) with gross investment income 314,504 of which 211,342 was realised + unrealised gains (interim:864-880, gross yield 5.58% vs 3.29%). FY2022 restated under IFRS 17 was 370,861 (kpis RevenueRestated); FY2022 as printed under IFRS 4 (804,388) is not comparable.
inputs.share_count_basis: 28,264,705,000 ordinary shares (A shares 20,823,530,000 = 73.7% + H shares 7,441,175,000 = 26.3%), unchanged since the 2007 A-share listing; weighted average 28,264,705,000 in both H1 2026 and H1 2025 (interim:3636). No share scheme, no convertibles, no treasury shares: basic = diluted (EPS 5.45 x 28,264.7 = 154,078 ties to attributable NI). A and H rank pari passu for dividends. Held FLAT.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO, the banks/insurers convention in this folder (1336.HK, 0998.HK, LGEN.L, PRU, 2378.HK). Borrowings RMB35,696M at 30 June 2026 (35,251 at FY2025) are capital supplementary bonds whose coupon sits inside finance costs (4,158 FY2025) already deducted from profit before tax, so the flows pay for them. Repo liabilities (kpis RepoLiabilities) are investment-operations funding, not corporate debt. Cash 147,822 is policyholder/portfolio liquidity inside RMB7.95tn of investment assets, not shareholder surplus. Solvency surplus (comprehensive 197.78%, core 156.80% at 30 June 2026, up from 174.01% / 128.77% at FY2025, interim:1150-1151) is the regulatory buffer and is NOT added back.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 dividends declared, RMB24,195M = RMB0.856/share (interim 0.238 + final 0.618; FY2025 AR Note 30 at :11000-11013) x 28,264.7M shares, 15.7% of attributable net profit of 154,078 but ~24% of a normalised ~100bn. This is the observed FCFE: the only cash a shareholder of a Chinese life insurer receives. DPS history: FY2019 0.73, FY2020 0.64, FY2021 0.65, FY2022 0.49, FY2023 0.43, FY2024 0.65, FY2025 0.856; H1 2026 interim 0.358 (+50% YoY, RMB10,119M, interim Note 15). An insurer's OCF-less-capex (CSV FY2025 OCF 459,925; capex not disclosed from FY2024) is policyholder premium float being invested, not free cash, so the identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income is deliberately not satisfied; reported_fcf is retained for auditability only.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 operating cash flow (no capex line disclosed from FY2024, so OCF is shown unadjusted). Not used by the model.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest revenue on financial assets (kpis InterestRevenueOnFinancialAssets, 128,286 FY2025) is the core investment yield on the policyholder float and part of normal insurer earnings. It is NOT stripped as non-operating; interest_income is 0 by design.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report and H1 2026 interim: no share-based payment, share option or share incentive scheme disclosed; kpis StockBasedComp/EquityAwardTaxes/ShareRepurchases are 0 in every period. State-controlled (China Life Insurance (Group) Company 68.37%) A/H-share insurer; SBC is genuinely zero, so house and street bases coincide and band_position is null.
inputs.buyback_note: No buybacks in any year; the count has been 28,264.705M since 2007.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are RMB (CNY) millions; the HKEX H-share quote is HKD. fx_rate converts MODEL -> QUOTE (the direction dcf_engine.py applies: iv_cny x fx_rate = iv_hkd): 1 CNY = 1.175 HKD, Yahoo CNYHKD=X 1.175 on 2026-10-22T03:30Z (HKDCNY=X 0.8502 inverted = 1.1762, consistent). Parity check against the Shanghai A-share 601628.SS (same economic rights): RMB33.66 x 1.175 = HKD39.55 against the observed H-share HKD22.54, i.e. the H trades at a 43% discount to the A (AH premium ~75%). That gap is the structural A/H discount Chinese insurers carry -- China Life's has long been the widest of the big four -- so the check proves the rate's direction and magnitude, not price parity. Canonical intrinsic_value / weighted_iv / entry_price are HKD, comparable to current_price, with *_cny siblings. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate. NOTE: scripts/sanity_check.py's historical_table() applies fx_rate in the opposite direction (known systemic bug, see memory); its printed historical multiples will be off by fx_rate^2 (~1.38x, small here) and must be hand-bridged, not trusted.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-22T03:28:03Z HKEX intraday (11:28 HKT, morning session) -- an intraday print, replace at the regular close; 52-week range 22.46-36.16, i.e. the price sits AT the bottom of its range, 38% below the high, ahead of the Q3 2026 results due around the end of October 2026
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY 10.0%, built in CNY because the flows are CNY: China 10-year government bond ~1.8% (mid-2026, approximate; no live CGB quote through the Yahoo chart endpoint) + beta ~1.25 x 6.5% China ERP = ~9.9%, rounded to 10.0%. One notch BELOW the 10.5% used for 1336.HK (New China Life) and 0998.HK because China Life is the scale leader (RMB7.95tn investment assets, 328M long-term in-force policies, Class A risk rating 32 consecutive quarters), its FY2023 trough ROE (9.65%) was shallower than NCI's, and its core solvency (156.8%) is 30pp stronger; equal to the 10.0% used for PRU and 2378.HK. The low risk-free rate does NOT pull the CoE lower because China's ERP is wider and the A/H structure adds a governance and capital-controls premium that H-share investors demonstrably price (43% H-discount). One rate across all three scenarios; capital-markets cyclicality is carried in the bear path and its 30% weight.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: lease liabilities ~RMB0.8bn (FY2025 AR maturity table :8469) against RMB7.6tn of assets; the IFRS 16 charge sits inside operating expenses already deducted in profit before tax.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests (RMB13,188M equity at FY2025, 2,474 of FY2025 net profit = 1.6% of PBT, 1,514 in H1 2026) are deducted via the cash_tax_rate_path, which is income tax + NCI as a share of profit before tax (FY2025: 25,077 tax + 2,474 NCI = 15.2%; H1 2026: 27,046 + 1,514 = 17.5%; FY2024 only 7.2% on tax-exempt dividend income and deferred tax). 15% used throughout. Revenue, margin and net income in the CSV are shareholder-attributable per the parser's note.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Life insurer FCFE at cost of equity via the engine route, net debt held at zero -- the same model as 1336.HK (New China Life, the direct comparable), 0998.HK, LGEN.L, PRU and 2378.HK; chosen over SKILL.md's BVPS x exit-P/B row for comparability with those names and because the dashboard slider engine needs component paths. Mapping: revenue = IFRS 17 total revenues; ebitda_margin_path = profit before tax / total revenues; cash_tax_rate_path = income tax + NCI (15%); da_pct = sbc = wc = 0; capex_pct_path is the RETENTION plug = margin x (1 - tax) x (1 - payout), so FCFE = after-tax attributable profit x payout ratio. The payout ratio and the normalised margin are the two levers that matter. The IFRS 4 -> IFRS 17 break (1 Jan 2023) halves the printed revenue series (FY2022 804,388 -> restated 370,861) and is an accounting event, not an operating one. FY2025 and especially H1 2026 earnings are PEAK-CYCLE: H1 2026 attributable NI 134,489 (+228.6%) carried RMB211bn of realised and unrealised investment gains on the A-share rally; the base case normalises FY2027 profit before tax to ~RMB115bn (NI ~98bn, ROE ~14%, between the FY2023 trough of 46bn at a 2.43% yield and the FY2024 107bn at 5.50%). Cross-checks: H1 2026 equity holders' equity 664,203 = RMB23.50/share (HKD27.61; price 0.82x book); embedded value 1,614,207 = RMB57.11/share (HKD67.1; price 0.34x EV); VNB 45,752 FY2025 (+35.7% on the new economic basis) and 38,167 H1 2026 (+33.7%), first-year regular premiums +24.7%; trailing dividend yield 4.5% at the quote. No 2628.HK_Analysis.json existed at build time, so the qualitative context is taken from the FY2025 AR and H1 2026 interim directly.

bear.narrative: An H2 2026 A-share drawdown turns the H1 unrealised gains (135.8bn) into losses: FY2026 revenue -15% to ~524bn, margin 22% (PBT ~115bn, meaning an H2 loss of ~48bn after the 163bn H1), NI ~98bn, DPS cut to ~0.69. FY2027: the 10-year CGB slides toward 1.5%, the guaranteed-rate cuts cannot reprice the legacy 3-3.5% guaranteed book fast enough, and negative-spread risk shows up as a 17% margin on ~424bn of revenue (PBT ~72bn, NI ~61bn, ROE ~9%, the FY2023 shape on a larger asset base). Growth 3-4% thereafter as bancassurance single-premium volumes fall away and persistency weakens. Core solvency drifts toward 130%, so the payout is held in the 30s and only reaches 40% by FY2035. Terminal min(Gordon 10%/2.5%, 12x FCFE) -- the H-share stays at ~0.25x embedded value.

base.narrative: FY2026: revenue +2% to ~628bn (H1 434.6bn on the A-share rally; H2 assumed ~195bn against a strong H2 2025 of 376.6bn, consistent with the share price falling to its 52-week low into the Q3 release) at a 29.0% pre-tax margin = PBT ~182bn (H1 163bn + H2 ~19bn), attributable NI ~155bn, roughly flat on FY2025; dividend ~26bn (DPS ~0.93, interim 0.358 already declared, payout 17%). FY2027: revenue falls ~20% to ~503bn as realised/FV gains revert toward a mid-cycle ~4-4.5% total return on ~8tn of investment assets, margin 23% -> PBT ~116bn, NI ~98bn, ROE ~14% -- the through-cycle level. FY2028 onward: revenue +5-6.5% with investment assets (+12%/yr historically, assumed slower as yields compress) and CSM release (VNB +35% FY2025, +34% H1 2026 on the participating-product shift and first-year regular premiums +25%), margin 23.5%, growth fading to 4.5% by FY2035. Payout rises 2pp a year from 28% to 45% as core solvency (156.8%) comfortably exceeds the regulatory floor and the SOE market-value-management push lifts distributions toward the 35-43% paid in FY2021-22. Tax+NCI 15%. Terminal min(Gordon 10%/3%, 15x FCFE = 6.75x earnings at a 45% payout) -- Gordon binds.

bull.narrative: H2 2026 markets hold: FY2026 revenue +10%, margin 30% (NI ~173bn), then the total investment return settles near 5% rather than 4% (the 'patient capital' equity allocation earns its keep, CGB yields stabilise), the margin normalises only to 25-25.5%, VNB keeps compounding 15-20% a year on participating products and ten-year-plus regular premium (+19% H1 2026) so CSM release outgrows the book, and growth runs 6-7.5% through FY2031. Core solvency rebuilds above 170% and the payout reaches 55% by FY2035. Terminal min(Gordon 10%/3.5%, 17x FCFE) -- a rerating toward ~0.6x embedded value, still below where the A-share trades.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: FY2025 and H1 2026 earnings are the most capital-markets-dependent in the company's history (211bn of H1 2026 gains on 163bn of PBT), the price has fallen to its 52-week low (38% below the high) into the Q3 2026 release, which says the market expects a weak H2, and the whole industry carries legacy guaranteed-rate spread risk against a ~1.8% CGB. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs a sustained ~5% investment yield, continued double-digit VNB growth, a tripling of the payout ratio and an A/H rerating together. 30/50/20 matches 1336.HK (New China Life) for comparability; China Life's lower equity leverage and 30pp stronger core solvency are reflected in a MILDER bear path (FY2027 margin 17% vs NCI's 13%) rather than a lower bear weight.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC zero): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
